The triage deep dive actionable queries step 1 is Query the source and any correlated host(s) for Windows Security Event ID 4624/4625 to retrieve username, logon type, source workstation, and IP; Event ID 4688 for process/user context; Event ID 4672 for privileged logons; and System event logs / EDR asset inventory for hostname and OS version. For hostname and OS, query AD/EDR asset inventory or run 'hostname' and '[System.Environment]::OSVersion' / 'Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | select Caption,Version,BuildNumber' on the implicated endpoint. For the likely account 'admin2', search domain controller security logs for matching authentication events and workstation name.. The triage deep dive actionable queries step 2 is Query EDR/Windows Security logs for adjacent authentications and remote activity from 192.168.20.14 and 192.168.10.14. Specifically inspect Security Event ID 4624 (successful logon), 4648 (logon with explicit credentials), 4672 (special privileges assigned), and 4778/4779 (RDP reconnect/disconnect) on likely source and target hosts; correlate with subnet membership to determine whether movement was lateral within the same tier or cross-tier. If available, run an EDR hunt for 'admin2' and session 6216976.. The triage deep dive actionable queries step 3 is Collect endpoint telemetry from the host 192.168.10.14: query EDR process creation events, Windows Security Event ID 4688, Sysmon Event ID 1, and PowerShell logs Event IDs 4103/4104 for the time window 2025-07-15 09:00:19 to 09:20:19 UTC. If you have shell access, run 'tasklist /v', 'wmic process get processid,parentprocessid,name,commandline', or 'Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | select Name,ProcessId,ParentProcessId,CommandLine' to identify spawned processes and parent-child lineage.. The triage deep dive actionable queries step 4 is Pull full endpoint process tree and network connection telemetry for 192.168.10.14 from EDR or Sysmon. Required sources: Sysmon Event ID 1 (Process Create), 3 (Network Connection), 5 (Process Terminate), 7 (Image Load), 10 (Process Access), 11 (File Create), and 22 (DNS). Also inspect Windows Security 4688 and PowerShell 4104 for command execution. If the host is Windows, run 'Get-Process | Sort-Object StartTime', 'Get-NetTCPConnection -State Established', 'netstat -ano', and 'Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{Id=4688; StartTime=...; EndTime=...}' to reconstruct the tree and check for privilege escalation, lateral movement tooling, or exfiltration utilities.. summary_text: 2025-07-15T10:01:02+00:00: RSA NetWitness ESA generated incident INC-52981 ('High Risk Alerts: ESA for 192.168.10.14') for repeated abnormal network activity from source IP 192.168.10.14 to broadcast destination 255.255.255.255 on UDP port 7989 (source port 38370), sessionid 6216976, with network analysis marked 'single sided udp' and direction 'lateral'. The alert context included the source trail 'admin2@192.168.20.14:50005', but no hostname, OS, process tree, PowerShell execution, file activity, or exfiltration evidence was present. Threat enrichment for 255.255.255.255 was non-malicious/low-confidence: AbuseIPDB abuse confidence 0, OTX pulse count 0, VirusTotal IP reputation -95 with 0 malicious and 53 harmless detections; no usable domain or file hash indicators were available. No decodable PowerShell EncodedCommand content was found. Overall, the incident remained a network-only suspicious lateral/discovery-style event affecting 192.168.10.14, with insufficient endpoint evidence to confirm privilege escalation or malicious process execution.
